_guide: Crew stories: one crew member's own little storyline, a step every few study sessions. A story starts now and then for someone who fits its "when" (usually a trait tag, see items.json), runs through its steps, then ends.

Fields: id (never reused), title, when (like lines.json: "crew.tags": "curious"), start, steps (two to five), end, and optionally keepsake (an item id from items.json, put in the stash when the story ends).

In the text, {Crew} is the person (capitalised), {crew.they} / {crew.their} / {crew.them} / {crew.themself} their pronouns, and {crew:is|are} picks the verb for their pronouns. Use the singular verb straight after {Crew}.

stories.title: Learning to paint
stories.start: {Crew} has found an old set of paints in a locker and decided, quite suddenly, to become a painter.
steps: {Crew} paints the view from the galley window. It is mostly blue. Everyone says it is very blue, in a nice way.
{Crew} tries a portrait of the ship. The ship has never looked so lopsided, or so loved.
{Crew} stops trying to paint what things look like and starts painting what they feel like. Something clicks.
stories.end: The painting goes up in the corridor where everybody passes it. Nobody can say what it is. Everybody stops to look.

stories.title: The letter
stories.start: {Crew} has been writing a letter home for weeks. It keeps getting longer instead of finished.
steps: {Crew} reads a page of the letter aloud at dinner, by accident. It is about the soup. The crew agrees the soup deserves it.
{Crew} adds a pressed leaf from the last world to the envelope, and a drawing of everyone aboard, labelled.
{Crew} realises the letter is really a list of things worth coming home to tell someone about. The list keeps growing.
stories.end: The letter goes into the mail drone at the next relay. {Crew} watches it go and looks lighter, the way people do after saying a thing out loud.

stories.title: The perfect soup
stories.start: {Crew} remembers a soup from childhood and is determined to make it again, out here, with whatever the ship has.
steps: The first try tastes of nothing. {Crew} writes "more of everything" on a scrap of paper and pins it to the wall.
The second try is too much of everything. The crew eats it anyway, slowly, with a lot of water.
{Crew} adds one strange root from a market on the last world. The galley goes quiet. Somebody has a second bowl, then a third.
stories.end: It is not quite the soup from childhood. {Crew} decides it is better: it is the ship's soup now, and it has a name.

stories.title: The night watch
stories.start: {Crew} has started taking the night watch every night, alone on the bridge, and won't say why.
steps: {Crew} keeps a notebook on the bridge at night. In the morning there is a new sketch of the stars in it.
Somebody finds out: {Crew} has been naming the stars on the night watch, one each night, after people {crew.they} {crew:misses|miss}.
{Crew} asks if anyone wants to stay up and meet the stars. Three people do. They are very tired the next day and do not regret it.
stories.end: The night watch has become a small club. There are blankets, a flask of tea, and a chart full of names.

stories.title: The great corridor race
stories.start: {Crew} has challenged the whole ship to a race down the main corridor, in socks.
steps: Training begins. {Crew} practises cornering at the galley door and knocks over the same chair four times.
Rules are argued over for an entire session. Socks are mandatory. Running is not. Sliding is encouraged.
Race day. Everybody falls over at least once. Somebody wins. Nobody can remember who, which is the best result.
stories.end: {Crew} is already planning next year's race, with a trophy made from a bent spoon.

stories.title: Afraid of the dark
stories.start: {Crew} admits, very quietly, to being afraid of the dark parts of the ship.
steps: {Crew} carries a glow stick everywhere. Nobody teases. A few people start carrying them too.
The crew strings little lights along the lower corridor. {Crew} walks it twice, just to see it.
{Crew} goes into the dark cargo hold alone to fetch something, and comes back holding it up like a trophy.
stories.end: The little lights stay up. Everyone agrees the ship looks better with them, and nobody mentions why they were put there.

stories.title: Lost and found
stories.start: {Crew} has lost something important and can't remember what it was, only that it was important.
steps: {Crew} searches every drawer on the ship. Things that were lost years ago turn up instead. One of them is a sandwich.
The crew helps. Nobody knows what they are looking for. It becomes a game: whoever finds the strangest lost thing wins.
{Crew} finds it in the last place: the inside pocket of a coat {crew.they} {crew:was|were} wearing the whole time.
stories.end: It was a note to {crew.themself}. It says: "You are doing fine." {Crew} keeps it somewhere easy to find now.

stories.title: A play in three acts
stories.start: {Crew} has written a play and intends to perform it, with the whole crew in it, whether they like it or not.
steps: Rehearsals in the galley. Nobody can remember their lines, so {Crew} rewrites the play to be mostly shouting.
Costumes are made from blankets and a lampshade. The lampshade is a crown now. It suits the ship's cat that isn't there.
Opening night. The audience is the ship's computer and a houseplant. It is a triumph.
stories.end: There will be a sequel. There will, everyone suspects, always be a sequel.

stories.title: The collection
stories.start: {Crew} has started collecting one small thing from every world: a pebble, a seed, a scrap of something.
steps: {Crew} builds a little shelf for the collection. It already needs a second shelf.
Somebody asks which is the favourite. {Crew} thinks for a long time and picks the most boring pebble, and explains why. Everybody understands.
{Crew} labels every piece with the world it came from and the day. It reads like a diary made of stones.
stories.end: The collection gets its own corner of the ship. The crew adds things to it now too, and asks first.

stories.title: The book
stories.start: {Crew} has decided to write a book about the voyage. It is going to be very long.
steps: Chapter one is about the ship's coffee machine. It is forty pages. {Crew} says it sets the scene.
{Crew} interviews everyone aboard. The interviews turn into long talks late at night, with tea.
{Crew} reads the last chapter aloud. It is about all of them. Somebody pretends to have something in their eye.
stories.end: The book is not finished. {Crew} says it never will be, because the voyage isn't, and that is the point.

stories.title: Something growing
stories.start: {Crew} has planted a seed from the last world in a cup on the windowsill, to see what it does.
steps: Nothing happens. {Crew} talks to the cup every morning anyway, quietly, about the weather.
A shoot. Very small, very green. The whole crew gathers round to look at it like it is a newborn.
It flowers: one small, strange, pale blue flower that smells of rain on a world none of them have been to yet.
stories.end: The cup becomes a pot, and the pot becomes a little row of pots. {Crew} has a garden now, sort of.

stories.title: Learning an instrument
stories.start: {Crew} has decided to learn the harmonica, and has decided everyone will hear about it.
steps: The first week is very loud. The crew starts a rota for who gets the earmuffs.
{Crew} learns one song properly. It is a sea shanty. It is played after every meal.
One night, very late, {Crew} plays something slow and quiet that nobody has heard before. Nobody says anything. Nobody needs to.
stories.end: The harmonica has a little case now, and the crew has started asking for the slow one.

stories.title: The morning routine
stories.start: {Crew} has started a morning stretching class for the whole crew. Attendance is not optional, says {Crew}.
steps: Day one: {Crew} is the only one there. {Crew} stretches anyway, loudly, so people can hear.
Day four: two people come, mostly for the tea afterwards. {Crew} counts it as a win.
Day ten: everybody is there, in pyjamas, half asleep, reaching for the ceiling together.
stories.end: Nobody admits it, but the mornings have become everyone's favourite part of the day.

stories.title: The apology
stories.start: {Crew} snapped at somebody over nothing, and has been quietly miserable about it ever since.
steps: {Crew} tries to apologise three times and ends up talking about the weather each time.
{Crew} bakes something instead. It is lumpy and burnt on one side. It is clearly an apology.
{Crew} finally says the words. They come out gruff and short. They are accepted immediately.
stories.end: Things are easy between them again, and maybe a little easier than before.

stories.title: The secret map
stories.start: {Crew} has found a scrap of an old star map in a second-hand book, with a little drawing of a door on it.
steps: {Crew} compares the scrap to the ship's charts for hours. Some of the stars match. Most don't.
{Crew} decides the map was drawn by somebody standing on a world, looking up. The question is which world.
{Crew} finds it: a world the ship passed long ago, where the stars would look exactly like this.
stories.end: There is no door, of course. But {Crew} pins the scrap above {crew.their} bunk and says it was never really about the door.

stories.title: Making a friend
stories.start: {Crew} has been sending messages to a radio operator on a far-off relay station. They have never met.
steps: The messages are short at first: weather, coordinates, the usual. Then {Crew} sends a joke. A joke comes back.
{Crew} and the radio operator start playing a very slow game of chess, one move a day, over thousands of kilometres.
The radio operator sends a recording of their station's little choir singing. {Crew} plays it for the whole ship.
stories.end: They will probably never meet. {Crew} says that's fine: a friend is a friend however far away they are.
